title: Demonstrators clash with police in Paris over living costs and public services
seoTitle: Paris cost of living protests and clashes

tea.why: Protesters are demonstrating against the rising cost of living, declining purchasing power, and inadequate public services.
tea.want: Demonstrators demand better living conditions, improved public services, and changes to government economic policies.
tea.changed: Oct 19: Paris police issued an overnight curfew in parts of the capital following widespread weekend riots and looting.

summary: Demonstrations over living costs and public services escalated into widespread unrest, clashes with police, arson, and looting in Paris and other French cities. The movement followed earlier student protests concerning school conditions. According to authorities, around 550,000 people participated nationwide, while trade unions claimed 800,000. Authorities deployed tear gas and water cannons in Paris as property and businesses were targeted. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu and President Emmanuel Macron condemned the violence, warning of legal consequences and introducing localized curfews.
response: According to authorities, police deployed tear gas and water cannons, and made numerous arrests. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu and President Emmanuel Macron condemned the violence, while Paris police instituted overnight curfews.

crowd.text: approximately 550,000 people participated in the protests

injuries.text: more than 150 police officers were injured

updates.text: Demonstrations and clashes with security forces erupted across Paris and other French cities.
Vandalism and looting were reported at commercial establishments, and a Paris synagogue was desecrated.
Paris police implemented an overnight curfew in specific areas to curb further disorder.
